items.title: Quantum Haar Wavelet Transform methods applications and hardware realizations in quantum computing
items.why_it_matters: Abstract Quantum Haar Wavelet Transform (QHWT) methods connect multiresolution analysis with quantum information processing through reversible averaging and differencing operations that can be implemented with comparatively compact circuits. Their localized basis functions, real-valued binary structure, and compatibility with hierarchical state representations make them attractive for resource-constrained quantum processing.

items.title: Can artificial systems become conscious?—Recursive embodied closure as an integrative framework
items.why_it_matters: Recent advances in artificial intelligence, connectomics, and computational neuroscience increasingly raise the question of whether artificial systems—or even pure computer simulations—could become conscious. Contemporary theories emphasize embodiment, predictive processing, homeostatic regulation, and continuous interaction between cognition, body, and environment rather than isolated computation.
